title: The client
about: `apps/cli` is `nemia` and `wf` as a person types them: a client of the api, which spawns the orchestrator's own CLI for every verb it has not moved.

terms.meaning: which way a command goes (`routeOf`, `apps/cli/src/route.ts`): `refused`, any command typed with `--local`, exit 2, naming it typed without; `api`, for a moved read (`READ_VERBS`: `show`, `closeout`, `ls`, the inbox's read, `watch`) asked of the api over HTTP, for the client's own verbs (`CLIENT_VERBS`: `get`, `apply`, `explain`, `propose`, `proposals`, `decide`) whatever else is typed, and for a moved command (`MOVED_COMMANDS`), its help included; `process`, for every other verb, a help of one, and a machine verb, run on the orchestrator's own CLI in a process of its own (`apps/cli/src/local.ts`); `forwarded`, a verb about the store only that path has, typed under a remote context, run on that CLI forwarded to the context's daemon.

a verb this client alone has, generic over every kind the api serves (`CLIENT_VERBS` in `apps/cli/src/route.ts`: `get`, `apply`, `explain`, `propose`, `proposals`, `decide`): no process answers it, so it asks the api whatever else is typed, says its own help. Each kind is called through one table, `KIND_CALLS` (`apps/cli/src/objects/kinds.ts`), and a word names a resource by discovery (`resourceNamed`, `apps/cli/src/objects/resource.ts`).

a named daemon this client asks, kubectl's way (`contextOf`, `apps/cli/src/context.ts`, proved by `apps/cli/contracts/context.contract.ts`): the client's config file, `${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-~/.config}/nemia/config.yaml` (mode 0600), holds each context's name, server and a person's token for it, and the one in use; `NEMIA_CONTEXT` names one for a single command. None named, or `local`, is this machine's store; a name the file does not hold is refused, exit 2, naming `nemia config get-contexts`. Written and read by `nemia config use-context <name>`, `set-context <name> --server <url> --token-file <file>`, `get-contexts` and `current-context`; the token is read from a file, never the command line, and no verb prints it.

a context that names a daemon on another machine (`Chosen` of kind `remote`, `apps/cli/src/context.ts`): the moved reads and the client's verbs ask its server with its token as `Authorization: Bearer` (`sessionHeaders`, `apps/cli/src/client.ts`, `WF_SESSION_TOKEN` first), this machine's lease is never read (`servedAt`, `apps/cli/src/where.ts`), no daemon is started here (`served`, `apps/cli/src/daemon.ts`), and a verb about the store only the in-process path has is forwarded (`forwardedEnv`), the words a moved read hands on among them (`handedOn`, `apps/cli/src/local.ts`); `nemia template export --factory`, which reads a store in process, is refused, naming `NEMIA_CONTEXT=local` (`factoryNotHere`).

the route of a verb about the store only the orchestrator's own CLI has, typed under a remote context (`routeOf`, `apps/cli/src/route.ts`, proved by `apps/cli/contracts/route.contract.ts`): that CLI spawned with the same words (`spawned`, `apps/cli/src/local.ts`) and the environment `forwardedEnv` makes (`apps/cli/src/where.ts`): the context's server in `NEMIA_SERVER` and its token in `NEMIA_SERVER_TOKEN`, never on the command line, and no `WF_ROOT`. It parses, checks and prints as ever and calls each command's endpoint on that daemon in place of its handler, refusing in its own words a command no endpoint serves. A help and a machine verb are never forwarded.

retired.card: distribution: the laptop's nemia calls a remote daemon for every store verb, forwarding what it refused

terms.meaning: a verb about the machine this client runs on, never a remote daemon's (`MACHINE_VERBS` in `apps/cli/src/route.ts`: `service`, `upgrade`, `up`, `tick`, `version`, `token`, `claude-token`, and the verbs that read and write this machine's files and no store, `template`, `frontmatter`, `admit`): it runs on the orchestrator's own CLI here whatever context is in use, a context the config does not hold included.

`nemia get <resource>[/<name>] [<name>] [-n <namespace> | -A] [-l <selector>]... [-o json|yaml|name]` (`apps/cli/src/objects/get.ts`): a resource's objects as a table (NAMESPACE with `-A`, NAME, STATE, AGE), or one by its name; `-o yaml` is what `nemia apply -f` reads back.

`nemia apply -f <file|->` (`apps/cli/src/objects/apply.ts`): each object a YAML or JSON file holds read where it is served, then made, written or left alone as `applyOf` says by what its kind takes, printing `<plural>/<name> created|configured|unchanged`; the one write the client moves. A missing Card is refused naming `nemia inbox add`, and a kind that takes no write naming `nemia explain`.

`nemia explain <resource>[.<field>]...` (`apps/cli/src/objects/explain.ts`): a resource's kind, version, scope and verbs from discovery, and its fields, each with its type and description, from the package's own OpenAPI document (`OpenApi.fromApi(Api)`), picked by `explained`.

`nemia propose -f <file|-> [-n <factory>] [--at approval|run-end] [--why <text>]` (`apps/cli/src/objects/propose.ts`): the objects a file holds, read as `nemia apply -f` reads them, each stamped with the `resourceVersion` served now where the file says none, sent as one `ProposalCreate` for the person, or an agent the person delegated to, to approve; `--undo <proposal>` proposes back the objects as they stood before it applied (`status.before`) and the removal of each it made. Prints `proposals/<name> <phase>`, `(widens access)` where it does, and its board page, `/factories/<factory>/proposals/<name>`.

`nemia proposals approve|decline <name> [-n <factory>]` (`apps/cli/src/objects/propose.ts`): a waiting proposal judged on its endpoint, printed as `nemia propose` prints one; a caller the api refuses (`Forbidden`, 403) or a token it does not take (`Unauthorized`, 401) exits 2 in the api's words, as every refusal.

`Authorization: Bearer <token>` on every request this client sends where `WF_SESSION_TOKEN` is set and not empty (`sessionHeaders`, `apps/cli/src/client.ts`), the token the orchestrator hands a session; none otherwise, which the api reads as the person.

refused, exit 2, whatever it is typed with (`routeOf`'s `refused`, `apps/cli/src/main.ts`), naming the command typed without it: no store is read in process any more, and `local` is this machine's daemon, reached through its api, started on demand where none serves.

a command whose words the client holds (`MOVED_COMMANDS`, `apps/cli/src/route.ts`, the names of `objects`' `COMMAND_WORDS`): parsed, helped, refused and printed in `apps/cli/src/commands/`, and run through the api under every context, its old path's runner deleted with the move: `workflows write`, `agents write` and `skills write`, whose files are read here and read into their spec by the api's `read`.

a command that finds no daemon listening at its store's lease starts one once, as a ticking command does, and waits until it answers `GET /api/health` before it asks, once (`apps/cli/src/daemon.ts`); where none comes up, or the start is off (`NEMIA_DAEMON_START=off`), it is refused, naming `nemia up` and `nemia service install`. Which daemon serves a store is the `url` of its lease, read in `apps/cli/src/where.ts` alone. The same probe reads the daemon's release, refused where it differs from the client's (`releaseMet`, `apps/cli/src/release.ts`).

a selector of the labels of the runs `nemia ls` lists or the cards `nemia inbox` lists (`team=core`), given again for another, of which one must take each; sent to the api as `labelSelector`, a query key given once per selector (`apps/cli/src/reads/table.ts`).

the server's `Labels` column of the table of runs or cards listed, `a=b,c=d`: the run's whole map (the person's keys, `workflow`, and `factory`, `default` for the default factory), the card's labels with its `workflow:` and `factory:`.

a column of one label key, after the server's columns of the table of runs or cards listed, its name the key in capitals and each cell the value of the row's object's label, empty where it has none; given again for another, in the order typed.

`nemia pair <url>`: this machine asks the server for a pairing, shows its code, waits for the person's approval there, and writes the context with the token the claim minted, 0600 and never printed (`apps/cli/src/pair.ts`); it then prints the `NEMIA_URL` line for Claude Code's plugin.

`nemia config headers`: the one verb that prints a token, as `{"Authorization":"Bearer …"}` on stdout for a harness's connection (the nemia plugin's `headersHelper`): `NEMIA_TOKEN` first, then the context's, then this machine's own (`apps/cli/src/context.ts`).
